 Cowboys take on Mean Green
 Published 2:51 pm Thursday, November 5, 2026
 By American Press Staff 
 Larry Johnson led McNeese State with 22 points on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026 in a 63-60 loss to LSU in an exhibition game at Townsley Law Arena. (Rodrick Anderson / American Press) 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 Larry Johnson and his teammates seem to be in midseason form after one game.
 Johnson scored a career-high 31 points in McNeese State’s 99-78 season-opening victory over Alabama-Birmingham on Monday in the Field of 68 tournament in Rock Hill, South Carolina.
 The Cowboys (1-0), the three-time defending Southland Conference champions, take on North Texas (1-0), another American Athletic Conference school, in an afternoon game in Denton, Texas. The Mean Green beat Southwestern Christian, a non-NCAA school, 122-50 in their season opener on Monday.
 McNeese was impressive in all phases of the game against UAB (0-1) — accurate shooting, especially from 3-point range, defensive pressure and transition, and rebounding.
 Rebounding was the major area of concern for head coach Bill Armstrong in the offseason. The Cowboys outrebounded the Blazers 33-26, led by Christian Nitu’s game-high six rebounds and dominated the paint 44-24.
 The Cowboys were sharp from the perimeter. Elijah “Choppa” Moore scored 15 points, all on 3-pointers. McNeese was 11-for-15 from 3-point range. Jaylon Dean-Vines came off the bench to score a career-high 17 points. He was 6 of 8 from the field, including 2-for-4 on 3-pointers.
 Email newsletter signup 
 McNeese also kept the tempo upbeat, getting 18 points off 14 turnovers and scoring 18 second-chance points. Jerrell Colbert provided the defense, making four of the Cowboys’ eight blocked shots.
 UAB hit five of its first six shots and led 15-6 after the opening 5 minutes. Then Johnson took over with nine consecutive points followed by a Moore 3-pointer to give the Cowboys an 18-15 lead after their 12-0 run. They continued the hot streak by hitting 12 of 18 shots in the final 10 minutes before the half for a 44-35 lead.
 The Cowboys connected on 14 of their first 17 shots during one stretch in the second half.
 In UNT, the Cowboys will meet a team with a blend of freshmen and veterans.
 Freshman Aeneas Alexander came off the bench Monday night to lead UNT with 22 points. Cash Chavis added 17 and Amar Amkou contributed 16 and nine rebounds. Je’Shawn Stevenson, who was voted the AAC Preseason Player of the Year, scored 15 points and dished out five assists.
 McNeese is the first of three consecutive UNT opponents who played in the postseason last year.
 NOTES: Johnson has scored in double figures in 31 of his 35 career games. … The Cowboys have won their last nine regular-season games dating to last season. … McNeese has won both meetings with UAB. … Today will be McNeese’s third game against UNT. The series is even with the Cowboys having won the last meeting 68-61 on Nov. 18, 2024 in Lake Charles. … UNT lost its two exhibition games. The Mean Green lost 62-60 at home to Northwestern State, and 67-64 at Colorado.
